ARABIC — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #5
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: ARABIC
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Phonological Awareness, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonological Awareness.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Phonological Awareness.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Phonological Awareness.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Phonological Awareness.

2. When practising Imitative speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Imitative speaking.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Imitative speaking.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Imitative speaking.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Imitative speaking.

3. When practising Selective Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Selective Listening.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Selective Listening.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Selective Listening.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Selective Listening.

4. When practising Conversational skills, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Conversational skills.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Conversational skills.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Conversational skills.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Conversational skills.

5. When practising Reading Fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Reading Fluency.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading Fluency.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading Fluency.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Reading Fluency.

6. In ARABIC, the best classroom habit is: (1 mark)
   A. Practise listening, speaking, reading, and writing every day
   B. Mix random languages with no purpose
   C. Avoid speaking to classmates
   D. Only memorise without using the language

7. When practising Reading for Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Reading for Comprehension.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for Comprehension.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Reading for Comprehension.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading for Comprehension.

8. When practising Speaking Fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Speaking Fluency.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Speaking Fluency.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Speaking Fluency.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Speaking Fluency.

9. When practising Intensive Reading: Short Stories, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Intensive Reading: Short Stories.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Intensive Reading: Short Stories.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Intensive Reading: Short Stories.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Intensive Reading: Short Stories.

10. When practising Active Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Active Listening.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Active Listening.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Active Listening.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Active Listening.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
11. In three clear sentences, explain Five Special Verbs فعَال ال َخم َسة َ أ and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

12. In three clear sentences, explain Numbers and Quantity العَ َدد َوال َمعُدود and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

13. In three clear sentences, explain Active Listening and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Phonological Awareness and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

====

1. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonological Awareness.

2. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Imitative speaking.

3. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Selective Listening.

4. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Conversational skills.

6. A — Practise listening, speaking, reading, and writing every day

7. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for Comprehension.

8. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Speaking Fluency.

9. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Intensive Reading: Short Stories.

10. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Active Listening.

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Five Special Verbs فعَال ال َخم َسة َ أ; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Numbers and Quantity العَ َدد َوال َمعُدود; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Active Listening; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Phonological Awareness; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
